headline: Discovering Shakespeare in the bush
summary: Cunninghame and Heller come in and another bull elephant falls. Roosevelt writes Lawrence Abbott, the Lodges and George Otto Trevelyan: he is reading Shakespeare with real pleasure for once in his life, faults Eliot's reading list, and favors an inheritance tax over an income tax.

events.detail: Cunninghame and Heller reach camp
Another bull elephant is shot
Letters on his Outlook pieces, books, the tariff and taxes

letters.topic: His editorials for The Outlook
Trip news, tariff, reading Shakespeare and Lowell, Eliot's book list, tax views
The hunt; thoughts on Macaulay and Carlyle

uncertain: The record cuts off the name of whoever shot the second elephant. The letter to the Lodges is also addressed to Nannie Lodge.

headline: Ten shots for one elephant
summary: Roosevelt kills a bull elephant at 70 yards; his sketch shows ten hits. Archie and Quentin sail home with an adult escort to start at Groton, Quentin's first year there, while Edith and Ethel remain in Europe.

events.detail: Kills a bull elephant
Archie and Quentin leave Europe for school at Groton
Edith and Ethel stay on abroad

headline: Cables about the Pole
summary: A quiet day by Roosevelt's diary. He writes William Foran about three cables concerning the rival Cook and Peary claims.

events.detail: Writes Foran on the North Pole cables

letters.topic: Three cables about the Cook and Peary polar claims

headline: Ted turns 22
summary: Roosevelt shoots a cow elephant. Ted marks his 22nd birthday, still at work for the Hartford Carpet Company in Connecticut.

events.detail: Kills a cow elephant
Ted's birthday; working in Hartford

headline: Into Meru
summary: Roosevelt goes to Meru.

events.detail: Travels to Meru

headline: To Lake Ingunga
summary: The safari moves on to Lake Ingunga.

events.detail: Marches to Lake Ingunga

headline: Rhino and elephant
summary: Roosevelt and Kermit kill a rhino and an elephant.

events.detail: Father and son take a rhino and an elephant

headline: A blank page
summary: Roosevelt leaves his diary blank for the day.

events.detail: No activity recorded

headline: Back to Meru
summary: Roosevelt returns to Meru.

events.detail: Goes to Meru

headline: Sunday writing
summary: Roosevelt writes at Meru Boma.

events.detail: Writes

headline: Outfitting the next safari
summary: Roosevelt spends the day organizing the safari for the next leg.

events.detail: Prepares the safari

headline: The party splits up
summary: Kermit and Tarlton head southwest for Lake Hannington while Roosevelt and Cunninghame make for the Guaso Nyero. An ailing Heller takes skins to Nairobi by donkey. Roosevelt shoots a crane in flight, and camp sits by a palm-lined brook full of monkeys.

events.detail: Kermit and Tarlton set out for Lake Hannington
Roosevelt and Cunninghame start for the Guaso Nyero
Heller, unwell, returns to Nairobi with the skins
Kills a flying crane, later identified in his book as a Kavirondo crane

headline: Congratulations for Peary
summary: Roosevelt and Cunninghame reach a branch of the Guaso Nyero and settle in for several days of hunting on the plains. He shoots a big oryx and writes Herbert Bridgman to pass his congratulations to Peary.

events.detail: Marches to a stream feeding the Guaso Nyero
Kills an oryx weighing about 400 pounds
Asks Bridgman to convey congratulations to Peary

letters.topic: Wants Peary congratulated on his polar success

headline: A dreadful miss
summary: Roosevelt flubs a shot at an ostrich and spends a beltful of cartridges on one distant oryx, plus two gazelles.

events.detail: Misses an ostrich; long shooting at oryx; two gazelles

headline: Ostrich, oryx and zebra
summary: Roosevelt gets a hen ostrich, a bull oryx and a big zebra, and writes notes on the ostrich.

events.detail: Kills an ostrich, oryx and zebra
Notes on ostrich

headline: The cock ostrich escapes again
summary: Roosevelt misses a cock ostrich a second time, but takes an oryx and a zebra and runs down another zebra on horseback.

events.detail: Misses an ostrich; kills oryx and zebra; rides one zebra down

headline: The ostrich at last
summary: Roosevelt finally gets his cock ostrich, and a giraffe after a gallop.

events.detail: Kills a cock ostrich and a giraffe

tr_quotes.text: Cock ostrich 85 yards. Giraffe, after Gallop, 180 yds.

headline: Guinea fowl, impala and oryx
summary: The bag includes two guinea fowl, an impala buck and a bull oryx, at the cost of another beltful of cartridges.

events.detail: Shoots guinea fowl, an impala and an oryx

headline: Camp by an abandoned boma
summary: The party moves to the Guaso Nyero close to the empty boma of Nyama Yango; Roosevelt shoots a waterbuck bull in the evening.

events.detail: Moves camp near the deserted Nyama Yango boma
Kills a waterbuck at dusk

tr_quotes.text: To the Guaso Nyero; near the deserted Boma of Nyama Yango.

headline: A serumik
summary: Roosevelt shoots a serumik at 90 yards.

events.detail: Kills a serumik

headline: African Game Trails goes to press
summary: Roosevelt kills another serumik and a buffalo cow, while Kermit hunts sable antelope alone. Roosevelt's African Game Trails begins appearing in serial form.

events.detail: Kills a serumik and a buffalo cow
Kermit goes after sable antelope by himself
African Game Trails starts its run as a magazine serial

references.title: Happy Hunting Grounds, by Kermit Roosevelt

uncertain: The record breaks off before naming where the serial appeared; earlier entries name Scribner's Magazine.
